recipes.name: Turkey Wild Rice Soup
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a soup pot over medium heat. Add onion and celery; cook and stir until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour, and cook until it turns a pale, yellowish-brown color, 3 to 5 minutes.
Gradually whisk in turkey stock until smooth and no lumps of flour remain.
Stir in carrot and bring mixture to a simmer. Cook, whisking constantly, until stock is thick and smooth and carrots are tender, about 2 minutes.
Stir in turkey, wild rice, almonds, salt, and pepper; simmer until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and half-and-half; heat until just below a boil. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Turkey Wild Rice Soup
raw_recipe.description: This turkey and wild rice soup made with tender leftover turkey in a creamy broth is easy to make and perfect for a comforting post-holiday meal.

review.reviewBody: I put in about a cup each of carrots and celery, finely dicing the carrots and cooking them along with the onions. Used whole milk rather than half-and-half. No almonds. So, pretty true to the recipe overall. It tasted amazing, and I will definitely make it again.

Excellent base recipe that really helped me in my first adventure making a wild rice soup. Going thru many of the comments I found very helpful. The vegetable portions for about 5 cups of liquid seemed too small so I too went for a cup of celery and finally chopped carrots. Added some more onion as well. I did all the veggies in the butter (carrots included) and added a few cloves of garlic just long enough to become aromatic. I added about another cup of turkey broth (used the carcass from my Christmas turkey to make it). Also with the wild rice I added a teaspoon of Better than Boullion chicken broth mix into the water for a bit more flavour. Other minor tweaks were some more salt, pepper, dried thyme and about 3 tsps of lemon juice. To finish it off I let it simmer in the slow cooker for a few hours to blend the flavours. Tastes great but my guess is it will even better tomorrow. Thanks again

This was wonderful. I did tweak a bit, but I'm not holding that against the recipie. I had 2 turkey legs, a turkey thigh and maybe 2 cups of "shreaded" turkey. I made my own stock by boiling the chicken parts for an hour, then strained them and let them cool. Then I pulled the turkey meat and tossed the bones. I use the broth to cook the rice and also for the soup base. I also used a grater to grate the celery, carrot, and onion. I think thata was a mistake because I didnt account for the extra water so I had trouble getting it to thicken. The taste is swesome though!!!

I used olive oil and butter when sauteing the vegetables along with minced garlic. I don't cook the wild rice first. I simmer for an hour and add more stock as needed. It's easier than cooking ahead of time. I also add half and half whisked with garlic cream cheese at the end for more flavor.

Fantastic! Easy to make and great for leftover thanksgiving turkey. You could easily make this with rotisserie chicken and chicken broth. I added minced garlic to the onion/celery sauté. I did put this in a slow cooker on low for 4 hours After whisking the broth into the rue and then added chopped portobellos to cook down. I added the half and half at the end along with a little more turkey broth. it was very good! I’ll be making it again and also plan to make a vegetarian version with veggie broth, zucchini and mushrooms.

We made a couple of minor changes. Like some others we diced the carrots and sauteed them with the onions and celery. Because my husband prefers soups not to be too stew like, I used 6 cups of chicken broth (instead of 4) and I added a little garlic powder. But, I think that what changed it the most is that I squirted in some Sriracha Sauce at the very end (hubby likes things spicy). I also used FF half and half. My husband said "this is the best thing I've ever made". Like a number of others we did not add the almonds.

Turned out just as I hoped it would. Perfect. I'm sure it is even better as written, I modified it a bit. Swapped the butter for 1/4 c of olive oil, used 2% evap milk, added 1/4 c grated parm cheese and some chopped green beans. Oh and I just chopped the carrots and added them in with the onions and celery. Cooked it on a low boil for about a half hour when everything was in the pot. Nothing like a great bowl of homemade soup like this one ????

This is now my favorite soup. As does everyone else, I made some adjustments. I chop onion and celery and sauté with butter. then add flour when they are just soft, add chicken bullion or, I prefer chicken stock. Then stir in flour and add turkey broth. Stir till thickened then add chopped carrot and simmer until almost tender, add turkey & rice. Simmer about 10 MN then add 1/2 & 1/2 & lemon. Awesome with freshly baked bread.

One word, DELICIOUS! I added fresh thyme, parsley, mushrooms,extra vegetables from list, only had 2 cups turkey broth so added 2 cans low sodium chicken broth. My husband was skeptical but after 1 bite loved it! 
 While rice was simmering, I chopped vegetables and cut up the cooked turkey. The celery and carrots were not mushy but had little crunchy which we liked. Will definitely make this again.- Dee
This soup recipe is delicious! I added a cup of each of the veggies and used chicken broth. I make this every year with my leftover Thanksgiving turkey.

Great recipe! basically started with doubling the recipe...why not? boiled 3 Turkey legs with salt, pepper. and 3 bay leaves to make stock and have Turkey meet (cooked legs had plenty of meat). Used margarine to saute onions and celery. Added garlic (again, why not?). As another reviewer mentioned, I added the carrots to then end of the saute to help soften quicker. if you don't have enough Turkey broth, just use low sodium chicken broth to make up the difference
 I used fat free half-and-half. I really liked the almonds. Doubled the lemon juice as it really brightened all the flavors. Yum!!!

This one is so good!! I love all the flavors. I didn't put the almonds or half-and-half, and it reminded me of Panera's wild rice soup. I also used chicken instead of turkey. It came out great! I'll definitely be making this again.
It tastes so good
Wonderful! Sauteedin butter mushrooms, no almonds. Chicken broth instead of turkey broth- no difference in flavor,
Good use of leftover turkey.

I made it with a few changes: I added 1 Tbsp Better than Bouillon chicken for didn't enhancement. I made it without the half and half due to dietary preferences. I threw in 3/4 cup frozen peas during the second to last step to add some vegetables. I cooked my rice in chicken as well. I REALLY liked this soup that way. Nice and thick, great flavors, and I still felt really good afterwards. I look forward to making it again.
Perfect, no changes
I used Bob's 1:1 gluten free all purpose flour for the win at our house.
I’ve made this for several years every Boxing Day /day after Thanksgiving - I follow the recipe to the letter, omitting the almonds
Came out tasting pretty good! I added more onion, celery, and carrots. I added mushrooms. I used more chicken broth than called for. I also used more flour than it called for. It is a very good soup!
